readerQuestion: How can I put useful Home Assistant controls on Android Auto, and tell a missing app, a connection problem, and a failed command apart?
directAnswer: Sign into the official Companion app on the phone, select Android Auto favorites, and first check a new software toggle from the phone on home Wi-Fi, over cellular, and on the parked car display. Then add an explicit Entrance lights on script. Away-from-home control requires a working remote path; a visible state update does not prove a tap succeeded, and favorites do not restrict the account's permissions.
originalContribution: Sections 2-4 supply a harmless Car practice helper and a three-stage diagnostic table that holds the target constant while changing the interface and network. Section 5 supplies an explicit two-light script, including copyable YAML and observed-result instructions. The troubleshooting table separates missing launcher entries, absent favorites, remote-connection failures, car-only command failures, and real-device/script problems. These are expected outcomes of an illustrative procedure, not reported hardware measurements.
limitations: No physical phone, Android Auto head unit, Android Automotive vehicle, lamp or live Home Assistant runtime was tested. The example YAML was parsed and checked against current action documentation. Vehicle support, list limits and app menus vary; the stated AAOS favorites limitation is documentation-based as checked on October 25. No response-time, universal compatibility or offline remote-control guarantee is made. The cover is a disclosed AI-generated illustration, not an installation photograph or app screenshot.
proofreadFixes: Final automated proofreading made the first troubleshooting row's expected result conditional on unused-app disabling actually being the cause; clarified resetting the practice helper through its browser control; replaced an assumed universal Customize launcher label with a check of the app's enabled launcher setting; added a direct Script reference beside the distinction between script running state and lamp state; and widened the first table column to avoid awkward mobile label wrapping. Verified that the cellular-only test precedes wireless Android Auto, whose Wi-Fi connection must remain enabled, and that the lighting script uses turn_on instead of toggle. The final pass retains four actionable TLDR bullets, defines entity/helper/script/VPN, places the Cloud subscription caveat beside that option, identifies the Add to shortcut's version prerequisite, separates Android Auto from Android Automotive, and keeps security devices out of the test. This was an automated editorial review, not a human or expert review.

claimChecks.claim: The official Companion app supports native Android Auto controls, including input_boolean and script entities; favorites are configured on the relevant phone. Android Automotive is a separate installation path with a documented Play Store favorites limitation.
The more-info Add to automotive-favorite shortcut requires Home Assistant 2025.12 or newer; menu naming and vehicle-imposed list limits are qualified in the article.

Android Auto has phone, vehicle, data and wired/wireless prerequisites beyond the Companion app's own minimum requirements; wireless use requires Wi-Fi support, so the cellular-only test is performed before connecting it.
Remote access requires a working transport. Home Assistant Cloud is a subscription option; a VPN must actually be connected. The car app does not provide a remote path automatically.
A Toggle helper stores an on/off value without physical hardware. The test helper is kept outside existing automations and reset to off before each trial, with on as the expected result.
The UI script creation path and saved action sequence match current documentation. The example targets two explicit placeholder light entities and requires substitution before use.
The script entity's on/off state represents whether it is running; an off state after completion does not mean the controlled lamps are off.
light.turn_on requests on, whereas toggle reverses state. The example has no delayed off step and does not prevent an independent automation from subsequently changing the lights.
Google documents Samsung phones disabling unused apps and reopening the phone app as a way to re-enable them. This is presented as a conditional cause, not a universal launcher fix.
View visibility controls tab display and leaves the URL accessible; hiding controls must not be sold as authorization.
The documented Users and Administrators groups both allow entity control; permissions are checked server-side. A non-admin account plus curated favorites does not establish room-only access.
